data.body:
REMEDIATION COMPLETE — both operations run against the live store and pushed.

Backup tag (created BEFORE the first write, unlike pre-a3-remediation which was stamped
mid-run): pre-b636-remediation -> 1433ebe8fb.
Rollback: git -C /Users/joeoakhart/rebar/.tickets-tracker reset --hard pre-b636-remediation

OP1 — fsck --repair-snapshots (the shipped path) over the latent population:
  SNAPSHOT_MISSING_SOURCES 505 -> 7; 498 tickets FIXED; 536 per-ticket REBUILD SNAPSHOT commits.

OP2 — explicit restore over the 214 already-damaged tickets. fsck cannot detect these: their
snapshots were rebuilt from surviving events so they no longer cite missing sources — the
evidence was destroyed by the rebuild that caused the loss. Driven from the impacted list
using the shipped restore_deleted_sources() + rebuild_snapshot_from_full_log().
  486 events restored, 214 rebuilt, 0 refused.

VERIFICATION (all 2038 tickets diffed against a pre-run baseline):
  closed 1619 -> 1831; in_progress 200 -> 9; open 130 -> 109.
  214/214 previously-regressed tickets read closed again.
  213 status changes total, 212 intended. The ONE other (556a open->in_progress) is a genuine
  concurrent 'ticket: CLAIM' commit by another process at 16:10 UTC, not a rebuild.
  fsck issues 515 -> 25.

Pushed to origin/tickets as 20a236fb6a.

RESIDUAL (deliberate, not failures):
  - 7 SNAPSHOT_MISSING_SOURCES remain: history cannot complete those logs, so the fail-closed
    guard refuses rather than rewriting them lossily. They are now visible findings instead of
    silent corruption. Ticket dirs: 316c, a6ea, bbc0, be08, c7c5, e0d4, f130.
  - 7 SNAPSHOT_STALE_CHANNEL, 6 MISSING_CREATE, 5 STATUS_FORK_RESOLVED are pre-existing/
    informational and out of scope for this bug.
  - fsck's authorship tally moved to 13927 signed / 17704 unsigned: the restored historical
    events are now counted. Not corruption, but worth a follow-up 'rebar verify-authorship'.
